full_judgment:
6. The plaintiff originally received as compensation Taka 9,856 for said acquisition. Ultimately, 0.0583 acre out of the requisitioned land was used for the road. Land measuring about 0.2435 acre remained unused. The plaintiff amalgamated said unused land with his land into 0.6281 acre and filled with earth and constructed 62 semi-pucca shops. Said shops were comprised of a supermarket under the name and style "Shamsur Rahman Boro Market". The plaintiff kept two shops in his possession and let out others. 

 8. It is further stated that when some of the tenants defaulted in the payment of rents, the plaintiff had to institute suits for their eviction. Defaulting tenants then approached the DCC and claimed in collusion with the DCC depositing rents in the Sixth Court of Assistant Judge at Dhaka. Then, the DCC at the instigation of defaulted tenants on 27-6-02 most illegally asked the plaintiff to show cause as to why he should not be evicted from the suit land. The representation submitted on behalf of the plaintiff was not still disposed of by the DCC. 

 10. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 in one set and defendant No. 4 alone contested by filing two separate written statements. 

 12. It was further stated that the plaintiff got recorded 0.3292 acre in his name in the DP Khatian No. 5392 behind the back of the DCC. Against said record of rights, an appeal was filed and decided wrongly against the DCC. Then, an application was made for review which was fixed for hearing on 25-6-03. Against the review order, the petitioner moved this Division and got a stay in Writ Petition No. 4522 of 2003. By transfer from the DIT the DCC became owner of the suit land. The plaintiff has got no right or title in the suit land and the suit was therefore not maintainable. 

 21. Mr Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahammad, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant No.4 in the later Rule, somehow adopted the submissions of Mr Rafiqur Rahman and submitted that the suit as framed was barred by limitation after acquisition and the Court of appeal below therefore fell in serious error in decreeing such time barred suit. 

 24. Lastly, he submitted that after requisition and acquisition, the plaintiff lost all right or interest in the suit land and the appellate Court committed serious error without notice of such legal consequence, which resulted in failure of justice. In support, he cited Bangladesh vs Samodra Narayan Mohajan and another 2006 BLD (AD) 145 =.11 BLC (AD) 226. 

 25. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party in both the Rules however, submitted that the acquisition case was not yet completed and the acquisition process was not yet final After release of the schedule 'Kha' land, the plaintiff possessed the entire suit land through tenants and two shops through his sons. 

 35. Trial Court found that 0.3018 acre out of the land of the plaintiff was acquired in aforesaid acquisition proceeding. Out of said acquired land, 0.0583 acre was used. In view of Exhibits 8, 8(ka), 10 and 14 land measuring about 0.1482 acre seemed to have been released and formal possession was delivered to the plaintiff. But though rest 0.953 acre was claimed to have been released but in support of such release no separate order was submitted. By Exhibit 14, the plaintiff deposited the money price of released land as was asked to. 

 38. The trial Court further found that the acquisition was not yet final. The suit was therefore, not barred by limitation. 

 39. The trial Court dismissed the suit as not maintainable on the view that after acquisition, there were development works and the record of rights was prepared in the name of DCC. I find no justification for such observation. The finding of the trial Court that there were development works on the suit land has got no basis since it is admitted that the suit land is now occupied by shops and there cannot be thought of and development works by the DCC in the shops, 

 47. Such view of the trial Court was reversed rightly by the appellate Court. Because, the decision of the trial Court is based on no authority. Earlier, wrong record of rights could be corrected by a mere application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In such proceeding, the aggrieved party was never required to establish title to get an order for correction of the record of rights. Reason is not far away to find. Record of rights does neither create nor destroy title. It is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared.
